He made me promise not to tell anyone what he’d done. Several months went by, and I moved across country, and all I could think about was him and the day we could be together forever. And I started to feel guilt because I thought *I* had sinned. (Repressive subculture, remember.)

He told his mom it was ME that had initiated the touching, and she believed him. I was devastated. I couldn’t quit crying. He’d torn my world to bits. For the next seven years, I longed for a healthy relationship with a man who was actually GOOD, but also I was terrified of men.

When my future husband first put his arm around me, I completely freaked out. It was hard to explain to him why I was so scared of him touching me. I was afraid of being used and discarded again, but I hadn’t found my voice yet to be able to talk about it.

I had some therapy sessions in 2013 and for the first time in 13 years I became able to think and talk about my abuser without flying into blind rage, spiralling into depression, or both. I wrote a letter to my abuser and I posted it online. I didn’t hide his identity.
